Subject: Increased latency + 500s in us-west-2 - urgent

Hi Irene —

Starting ~15:40 PDT we started seeing a significant spike in token latency (3–5x) and intermittent 500 responses against Redwood's hosted endpoints in us-west-2 (appears concentrated in one AZ). Affects our inference pipeline; tails are very long and throughput has dropped by ~35%.

We pulled a few traces and there are repeated re-tries from the client and elevated queue times. Attaching sample trace and a small heap snapshot we captured. Can you confirm whether this is on your side and what the ETA is for mitigation? Our SLAs are impacted and our customers are starting to open tickets.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Increased latency + 500s in us-west-2 - urgent

Quick triage (first pass):
- Scope: concentrated in one AZ (us-west-2b) — we’re seeing TCP connection queuing on the NLBs and elevated GPU scheduling latencies on a subset of Dedicated nodes. Hosted pool has elevated queue times but not full outage.
- Likely proximate cause: a noisy tenant in the Dedicated pool causing CPU/IO pressure on the NLB and backend proxies; autoscaler didn’t react fast enough due to request burst shape.

Immediate mitigations I’ve executed (16:32 PDT):
1) Ingress policy: temporarily route new incoming requests from Kiln to us-west-2 but prefer eastus fallback (soft-failover) for heavy requests.
2) Emergency horizontal scale: spun an extra Dedicated shard (+4 GPUs) in west and east; should relieve scheduling pressure in ~6–9m.
3) Applied short-term per-tenant rate limit for suspected noisy tenant in west to reduce NLB queuing.
4) Enabled prefix KV cache for Kiln to reduce token regen load by ~20%.

Observed effect: queue times dropping at 16:44 PDT; error rate dropping but still elevated (500s now ~1.2% vs 4.5% at peak).

Attachments: mitigation_timeline_20260802.pdf (internal timeline)

Next steps I propose: keep east failover in place for 45–90m, monitor token tail latencies, if error rates >1% after 30m open rollback to older model variant for traffic that is latency-sensitive.

—Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

Quick summary for execs: Kiln (Tier 1 customer) reported latency spike and 500s concentrated in us-west-2 AZ starting ~15:40 PDT. We applied ingress routing adjustments favoring eastus fallback, emergency scale (+4 GPU shard), and per-tenant rate limiting. Error rates reduced from ~4.5% -> ~1.2% over ~12m.

Customer impact: throughput degraded ~35% at peak; some customer tickets opened. Rishi expects stabilization within 30–45m; full mitigation and verification 60–90m. Postmortem in 48h.

Decision request: Kiln is requesting guidance on credits for the period of degraded service. Recommend we offer a goodwill credit (one week of hosting fees for affected traffic) pending postmortem confirmation. Need approval to communicate.

PagerDuty: PD-87214 (open). HubSpot: Company 7890.

Thanks —
Irene
